classes.b: well-founded suspicion the package data cannot settle
classes.c: policy choice to disclose / principle contradicted by data

findings.title: One recipient receives 31.6% of all value and 43.1% of all money; with two addresses funded from the same bridge-in 34.9%; related-party status not disclosed; LP block outside the previous independent check
findings.remedy: Disclose whether the top recipients are related parties and show totals with and without them; extend the independent check to LP owners incl. v4; confirm identity of the second LP before paying ETH.

findings.title: Window A refunds go mostly to buyers who traded after the hack was public (Blockaid alert 18:28:27 UTC) and at crash prices; 24 refunded owners also burned purchased WGNK into the bridge
findings.remedy: Disclose the cut-off sensitivity; vote separately on the tranche after the first public alert or apply the ladder from that alert; exclude from money refunds WGNK the buyer burned into the bridge.

findings.title: 'Nobody profits from the hack' is contradicted: 142 owners keep trading gains
findings.remedy: Drop the wording or state the number and publish the list; cancel these owners' queued bridge burns (537,967.99 WGNK).

findings.title: Post-hack bridge burns and 'voided' WGNK are void only on paper (queued BRIDGE_PENDING records, tokens still transferable)
findings.remedy: Make cancellation of post-hack pending burns and replacement/freezing of the old WGNK contract explicit preconditions of payout; define treatment of trades after T2.

findings.title: Protocol top-up overstated: bridge escrow GNK not counted as a source; returned ETH held unconverted
findings.remedy: Add the escrow to the sources of funds; convert the stablecoin part of the returned ETH immediately; restate the top-up.

findings.title: Clusters are keyed and paid at the alphabetically smallest address, not the address that held the tokens or paid the money; cluster rule has no minimum amount and ignores direction
findings.remedy: Pay GNK to the address holding at the snapshot and money to the paying address; use clusters only for netting; require a minimum amount and the holder's signature for merges.

findings.title: Bridge-ins in flight (GNK locked on Gonka, WGNK never minted) are not in the register
findings.remedy: Publish the status of every unmatched mint request and return locked GNK to the Gonka signer.

findings.title: Third-party settlement: refund currency and payee are assumptions (solver/relayer inventories)
findings.remedy: Pay these refunds only against a signed claim showing the paying leg.

findings.title: Window-B netting: sale proceeds inside an ignored net loss are not deducted
findings.remedy: Deduct window-B proceeds from sales of earlier inventory, or state the exception.

findings.title: Money-only Uniswap v4 liquidity operations are not scanned (transaction set built from WGNK Transfer logs)
findings.remedy: Collect transactions by pool and PositionManager events as well.

findings.title: 'Pending pre-hack burns' are mostly stuck bridge records 41-135 days old
findings.remedy: Disclose; cancel the old bridge records so they cannot be delivered twice.

findings.title: Deliverability: recipients that never signed or are contracts; unreliable status column; unassigned pre-hack WGNK
findings.remedy: Define the claim procedure; check code at each address; decide on WGNK held by settlement contracts.

findings.title: Option 1 <= 2 <= 3 is false for one owner
findings.remedy: Check monotonicity on payouts, not on M; floor option 3 at option 2 per currency.

findings.title: Purchases paid in untracked tokens and unpriced liquidity positions (confirmed small)
findings.remedy: Accept individual claims with a price reference.
